invariants: No new dependency on a running product instance: the workbench must still open with the product stopped.
No phase or token GOV.ORCH.4 defines changes meaning.
report.merge_gate: The worker opens the pull request and does not merge it.
report.objective: The workbench looks nothing like the product it orchestrates, and it forgets everything it finishes. Give it the products own palette and an archive that keeps completed movements instead of losing them.
output_contract: A SESSION CLOSE on the relay as one NEXUS_SESSION_PACKET.

recommended_reasoning.reason: One surface, its stylesheet and one new section; the palette is quoted and the state vocabulary named.

requirements: Do not duplicate the palette. Generate or import it from the products token file so a change there reaches the workbench.
The archive is collapsed by default. The live list stays the first thing on the page.
risks: Retyping the palette into the stylesheet would satisfy the screenshot and reintroduce the drift this movement exists to remove.

in: Restyle the workbench against the products palette. Take the values from ui2/frontend/src/theme/m3Theme.ts rather than retyping them: a second copy of a palette is a second source of truth and will drift.
Map each movement phase to the products own state vocabulary from tone.ts. Honour its rule: red means real failure, never an ordinary terminal state.
Add a collapsed archive section at the foot of the workbench listing completed and cancelled movements, so a finished movement leaves the live list without being lost.
The archive reads whatever record survives; if a completed movement leaves no record at all, say so in the pull request rather than inventing one.
out: Changing what the workbench measures. GOV.ORCH.4s observability tokens, stuck detection and phase vocabulary are untouched.
Any change under ui2/. The palette is read from there and not modified.
The product wordmark. A separate movement carries it once the Product Owner has chosen a candidate.
